svg.title: Roadmap Arc BPMN
svg.desc: BPMN 2.0 process diagram of how a roadmap-orchestrator arc runs as of 1.0.0-dev.32: a top-level collaboration of three pools (owner, architect, executor with lanes for the scheduler, unit pipeline, holistic layer, milestones and demo, flow loop, and fault event sub-processes), an owner event sub-process for optional estate compaction whose approved decisions (_next/compaction.md) the next Phase 0 applies, followed by expanded sub-process panels for bootstrap, Phase 0, the unit lifecycle, lanes, parks and holds with propagation, deflake and environments, milestone walk and demo, lens audit and checkpoint, the flow loop, the architect's wake handling, arc-wide holds, close-out, PR and chain, and a legend.
svg.text: Executor (detached Node process under a supervisor; one per host)

text.tspan: Bootstrap [+], expanded: architect, once per repo (when .roadmap/corpus.md or chain.k is missing); on its own branch, never the integration branch
Phase 0 [+], expanded: architect, each arc, in session. The skill states what each step must achieve; the method (subagents or not) is the architect's.
Unit lifecycle [+], expanded: executor, one instance per admitted unit

Bounds (a unit's own limits override): chargeable 3 · certifications 4 · redirects 2 · reviseRounds 2 · candidateReds 1 · retries 1 (one uncharged retry per stage) · judgment deadline 45 min · fresh build 180 min · smokeRounds 1 · smokeRuns 2. Link events (arrow) jump within this panel; error end events are parks, escalation end events are holds (the way back is the "Parks and holds" panel).
Lanes [+], expanded: executor, in a detached checkout of the salvage SHA
Lanes-stage same-commit flake: uncharged fix, allowance unchanged; never mint from an own-commit flake. Certification reds use the allowance loop below; other outcomes route to Unit lifecycle.
Spec series: the spec's lanes (cadence build | unit), previous reds first, then cadence, serially under reservations
Parks and holds: the way back [+], expanded; and the code-minted work around units (dev.17)
Left: executor and architect together (message events mark the hand-offs). Right: three executor processes that mint or gate units.
Propagation (dev.17): when a requirement or contract changes mid-arc
Flaky ledger and deflake units (dev.21): mint only from integration-tip flakes
Costed environments (dev.17): plan.environments {name: {probe, up?, down?, idleMinutes?}}
Milestone walk [+] and Demo promotion [+], expanded: executor (holistic arcs only)

A milestone is the smallest end-to-end experience (web flow, API, CLI, SDK, bus, CI/CD, config, docs): a design unit (risk high, first), references (whole into every plan-check, build and gate prompt of its units and into the walk; 512 KiB cap), bringUp, journeys (via browser | shell, step and time budgets), resources.
Lens audit [+] and Checkpoint [+], expanded: executor's holistic layer
Holistic jobs run one at a time, in the order pack review, baseline, checkpoint, walk, propagation revision, polish revision / compare, audit.
Checkpoint (one job at a time; triggers in order: parks first)
Flow loop [+], expanded: tunes how the arc runs, never what it measures (code diagnoses, a model only proposes)
Flow stays on in dev.17 arcs (any recorded role set). Stations include scaffold and poc. Tests, witnesses, arc lanes, judgment seats, lenses and the vision are the ruler and never levers.
Handle the wake [+], expanded: architect, in session (one roadmap watch --actionable per arc)

The wait: watch runs in the background into <inputs>/<arc>/watch.jsonl with a Monitor on tail -F; on restart it uses --from <last seq>; it never polls status. Every intervention and every arc-wide lever is logged to roadmap-inputs/skill-feedback.md.
Arc-wide holds [+], Close-out [+] and PR and chain [+], expanded
Arc-wide holds: executor, after ready, before the first admission
How a roadmap-orchestrator arc runs (1.0.0-dev.23), in BPMN 2.0

Top level: the collaboration between the owner, the architect (Claude in the owner's session) and the executor. Every collapsed sub-process [+] is drawn expanded in a panel further down. Legend at the bottom.

Charged (counts toward 3): every fourth certification red; smoke survivors, gate revise, candidate red,
transient violation. Uncharged: first three certification reds, lanes flaky; redirect, PoC, scaffold retry, base-red, preempted,
finding-blocked, conflict / resolve; every env or retryable park, every hold, executor-fault. No model escalation of the
builder (D4 retired): the Opus advisor is how a hard round gets the stronger model.
Ready: the unit is active; every after dependency merged (following the lineage); contingent edges resolved; every
milestone node it descends from passed; its next stage admissible. Admission boundaries sit before prepare, reproduce,
plan-check, scaffold, poc, build, lanes, gate and candidate (pause, drain and constraints re-checked); chain stages
(quiesce → evidence → salvage → teardown, ff → snapshot) run regardless of pause or drain.
Holds on a unit not yet started: known-defect{id, fixUnit} (waits at prepare); deflake{deflake, lane}; propagation{unit, target,
stale} (at gate admission); host-pressure; a polish candidate's compare. Arc-wide constraints: a usage-limited or parked
backend blocks the stages calling it; a tripped host breaker blocks builds and lanes; base-red blocks candidates;
recovery-required, log-corrupt and supervisor-crash-limit block all admission. Calibrated CPU; explicit cpu overrides.
Defaults: judgment 1, build 4, build-cadence lane 2, others 4. Builds hold CPU only; pressure brake holds new workloads.
plan-check reads the spec, the vision (read-only, non-directive), milestone references, PoC reports and stale links; it
never touches costed environments, candidate or batch lanes. approve carries a design record: changes, interfaces,
failureModes (each proven by a test item or untested: reason), clauses, breaks {tests, docs}, kind module | integration,
experiments, newSystem, verification (deflake units). Oversize: two or more systems over 200 lines each, or an estimate
over the gate's inline budget (~1310 lines). visionConflict entries become P3 findings for the checkpoint, never a redirect.
Bound only as far as code can check: an undeclared contract touched → a risk trigger, and the gate is told
<undeclared_contracts>; an unlisted test or doc change by the build → a builder departure appended to the spec's
decisions, never refused. Design-record change paths outside the scope become a scope-growth proposal (dev.17).
Stale links (dev.17 propagation): an approve or redirect must answer each one, updated or confirmed, with a reason. A
unit already past its plan-check re-opens at plan-check at its next boundary (stale-reopened).

Proportional review (dev.17). A blocking finding must name a defect: incorrect-behaviour | contract-violation | security | requirement-unmet | test-inadequate | data-loss; otherwise the answer is refused through

the repair turn. test-inadequate: a test cited as proof does not verify it (an uncited imperfect test never blocks). Comment and doc findings ride along: never a revise; debt if they name a drag, else released.

Findings ledger (R-n, anchored at file blob): blocking findings open; a settled finding (fixed, released, banked, or a dispute ruled) cannot block again unless its blob changed. The builder may dispute in

decisions.json; the next gate rules once, finally. Delta re-gate: an approval records file blobs; a later gate at the same spec revision reviews only changed files plus files citing a moved contract or requirement;
nothing changed and nothing moved → delta-empty, no call, approved again.
Scope-only re-entry: carry the latest approval only at its exact approved head, with no later failed gate and an otherwise equivalent spec (design records may differ).
Its diff must pass the new pinned scope check; only delta-empty carries, with no judge call. Otherwise review in full.

Inputs: the spec with its design record, contracts and rulings, the lane ledger, witness and smoke checks, the scope plus growth and reverted paths, plan-check notes. Large diff: at least seat high (frontier,

which every tier now is), and a clusters map covering every changed path once. Propagation hold: no unit linking a changed requirement or contract, or whose design breaks a re-witnessed file, is admitted to
its gate until the propagation unit merges or is cut.

The tested head is the published head; the PR diff holds product changes plus living .roadmap/ docs only. Other publications on the slot: a docs publication docs{pub} (rulings, contracts, rendered .roadmap/

files, vision edits) outranks unit publications and preempts a candidate before green; a repair batch batch{finding} publishes the approved repairs of one finding (or repairs holding each other in a P1 cycle) as
one candidate. Candidate suite lanes: a lane with no systems always runs, an unmapped path runs every lane, a docs-only diff runs none. Transient check: only the effective scope plus ruled paths, no

Lane mechanics. One reuse key (lane, laneRev, envId, inputSha), where inputSha covers the lane's systems' paths, or
the whole tree minus docs; only a clean certified pass is reused. Test-only runs: with a testArgv, only the changed leaf test
files run. Stochastic lanes: {runs, minPasses}, k of n, never flaky. Never quarantine or skip a flaky test. Batch lanes never
sit on the merge path. timeoutMin → timeout red; absent → six-hour deadline backstop (blocked).

again); routing-changed → restore the seat, then resume; usage-limit → resume --backend <b> once it resets.

Break vs deviation. A break would force rework if fixed later (the journey cannot be completed, the interface contract is wrong, or a declared floor is violated): a P1 that keeps the
milestone node unpassed, so DAG descendants wait. A deviation (copy, visuals within tokens, layout, docs disagreeing with a correct contract, log text) is a P2, repaired alongside; it
does not hold dependents. Any unweighed finding gets an immediate checkpoint, again under a new vision even after a decision or skip; its round stays open for repair / re-walk after merged code.

bundle-request is the architect's: ack --choice apply | reject (or acknowledge | decline). Still open at close-out, code declines it and turns it into an amendment. Owner-requests (irreversible, over $10, legal; also a
vision, resource, config, gc or ref op; a new lane program) apply nothing and raise a blocking item.
Non-bundle drift: throttle to 60 min from last audit start while work remains.
Held drift joins the next audit (any fresh trigger can carry it).
Bundle drift and drift after work ends are never held.

Admit classes (corpus arcs): repair and oversight always admitted; opportunity limited to one per arc, needs its witness, gets one follow-up repair; unrelated, over-budget, unwitnessed and follow-up-overrun admits
are dropped and become corpus amendments.

Divergences: one per act departing from the target, an obligation, the plan or a contract, and one per interpretation, with preimages; non-blocking, rolled into a divergence-digest; the architect can reverse <D-n> or
apply. Amendments are dispositioned at the next Phase 0; the corpus is never edited mid-arc except for an owner's answer.

Tail brakes (dev.13): a P3 is never debt. Regress brake (findings about code written by finding-origin units) and settled brake (every milestone passed, every other unit merged or cut, below-P1 findings bearing on
no non-negotiable clause): an admit spawns no unit, P2s are released (or banked if ruled deferred). Neither touches P1s, obligation-broken or walkthrough findings.

Stations: each merged unit's lead time is cut into stations (service time and the wait in front of each stage, the integration slot, time held). Constraint: over the last ten merges, the station with the largest mean wait in front of it when that wait is ≥

10 % of lead time, else the largest mean service time; host:cpu first when the cpu is saturated. Levers: concurrency, resource-pool, suite-lane (test-runner flags), sequence, build-class, host. Verdict: the next five samples against the five before
Apply at once: the Phase-0 record marks it answered; corpus edit on the work branch plus re-pin;
census and obligations updated (apply --ruling for any weakening); a unit added if code is needed

svg.text: Container setup refreshes roadmap on PATH each skill session. After startup and completion, the architect shares a pinned roadmap tui command; the viewer is read-only.

text.tspan: The check-in also states the estate's size (rules,
obligations, rulings, open debt) and recommends
decision was applied in the last three arcs.

estate-compaction when no decision was applied
Estate compaction (optional; any time, while an arc runs or between arcs)

Certification loop [+]: after build report → quiesce → evidence → salvage → teardown → executor lanes
Builder uses targeted checks; no full-lane rehearsal. Spec and fast-suite series run previous reds first, then cadence; each stops on red.
limits.certifications and limits.chargeable override defaults. Any charge resets the allowance; a flaky fix neither consumes nor resets it.
Per-lane timeoutMin → timeout red through the red-lane protocol. No limit → six-hour deadline backstop (blocked); stall remains independent.
CPU: explicit override, else calibrated p90 demand from the last 10 qualifying runs (≥30 s, ≥3 samples), bounded by defaults; reservation records the basis.
Pressure brake: saturated host + CPU already held → wait.
Judgments exempt; lone workload progresses. Release/cooling → retry.
TUI/status: allowance, ordered lanes, held estate, CPU basis/use, token wait.
